Sodium Iodide/tert-ButylACHTUNGTRENNUNG(dimethyl)silyl Chloride-Induced
Isomerization of 2,3-Allenols to 2( E)-Enals
Rong Zeng, a Zhichao Ma, a Chunling Fu, a,* and Shengming Ma a,*
a Laboratory of Molecular Recognition and Synthesis, Department of Chemistry, Zhejiang University, Hangzhou 310027,
Zhejiang, People/C29s Republic of China
Fax : (+ 86)-21-6260-9305; e-mail: fucl@zju.edu.cn or masm@sioc.ac.cn
Received: September 13, 2013; Revised: December 30, 2013; Published online: March 17, 2014
Supporting information for this article is available on the WWW under http://dx.doi.org/10.1002/adsc.201300835.
Abstract: Through an unexpected C =C bond migra-
tion, 2( E)-enals were efficiently prepared highly ste-
reoselectively in moderate to good yields via the
sodium iodide/ tert-butylACHTUNGTRENNUNG(dimethyl)silyl chloride (NaI/
TBSCl)-mediated reaction of the easily available 2,3-
allenols. Based on a careful mechanistic study, in-
cluding control experiments and deuterium-labeling
experiments, an electron-withdrawing substituent
group in the 4 position has been proven to be crucial
and a possible mechanism has been proposed.
Keywords: allenols; electrophilic addition; migra-
tion; oxidation; a,b-unsaturated aldehydes
Introduction
a,b-Unsaturated aldehydes are an important class of
chemical compounds because of the wide existence of
this unit in nature, the extensive use in food, cosmetic
and pharmaceutical industries,
[1] and for being valua-
ble intermediates in organic synthesis. [2] Therefore,
there have been many practical methods for the syn-
thesis of the this type of compounds.
[3–9] On the other
hand, as an equivalent to TMSI, TMSCl/NaI reagent
has been widely used in synthetic organic chemis-
try.
[10,11] In 1989, Y . Ishii et al. reported a facile iodina-
tion of allylic alcohols with the NaI/TMSCl/H 2O
forming allylic iodides (Scheme 1). [11b] However, when
we applied this set of reagents to 2,3-allenols with an
electron-withdrawing group on the allene unit,
[12,13]
2(E)-enals substituted with an electron-withdrawing
group at the 4 position were unexpectedly formed
upon the treatment with NaI and TBSCl (Scheme 1).
Herein, we wish to report the details of this transfor-
mation.
Results and Discussion
At the beginning of our work, the reaction of per-
fluoroalkyl-containing 2,3-allenol 1a, prepared follow-
ing the known procedure,
[14] with NaI and TMSCl was
carried out in MeCN at room temperature with the
purpose of preparing the corresponding allenyl
iodide. Surprisingly, instead of forming the expected
allenyl iodide product Z-3a, a new product was
formed unexpectedly. Interestingly, the
1H/13CN M R
and IR analysis of this product indicated the presence
of an aldehyde functionality. Further study of the
mass spectra led us to the conclusion that this product
should be 4-butyl-6,7,7,8,8,9,9,9-octafluoro-2-phenyl-
2(E),5(Z)-nonadienal 2a (Table 1). The configuration
of the double bond in the 2-position was determined
by a NOESY analysis.
[15] Having established the iden-
tity of 2a, the solvent effect was then examined with
2.0 equiv. each of NaI and TMSCl at room tempera-
ture to optimize the reaction yield (entries 1–6,
Table 1): toluene gave a similar result with benzene
(entries 1 and 4, T able 1); using THF as solvent, the
reaction was messy (entry 3, T able 1); MeCN re-

In addition, this reaction did not proceed in the ab-
sence of either NaI or TMSCl (entries 7 and 8,
Table 1). The yield of 2a could be improved to 66%
when 1.5 equiv. of TBSCl were used, and further in-
creased to 72% yield when the concentration of 1a in
MeCN was adjusted to 0.1 M (entry 13, Table 1).
Thus, we defined the experimental protocol for the
migrative oxidation of 4-electron-withdrawing group-
substituted 2,3-allenols with 2.0 equiv. NaI and
1.5 equiv. TBSCl in MeCN at room temperature as
the standard reaction conditions for further study.
With the optimized conditions in hand, the scope of
this reaction was studied, and the typical results are
summarized in Table 2. Differently substituted 6-
fluoro-6-perfluoroalkyl-2,3,5(Z)-trien-1-ols 1a–1n
were successfully applied in this reaction to afford 6-
fluoro-6-perfluoroalkyl-2(E),5(Z)-dienals 2a–2n in
moderate to good yields with high stereoselectivity.
The substituent R
1 could be alkyl groups, such as n-
butyl (entries 1–10, T able 2) or n-hexyl group (en-
tries 11–13, Table 2); the R f group could be n-C3F7
(entries 1–8 and 11–13, T able 2), n-C5F11 (entries 9
and 10, T able 2), or CF 3 (entry 14, T able 2); the R 2
group may be phenyl (entries 1, 9 and 11, Table 2),
substituted phenyl (entries 2–6, 10, 12 and 13,
Table 2) or a thienyl group (entry 7, T able 2). The re-
action of substrates with R
2 being an electron-donat-
ing phenyl group (entries 2–4 and 12, T able 2) gave
better results than that of the phenyl (entries 1, 9, 10
and 14, T able 2) or those with an electron-withdraw-
ing group on the phenyl ring (entries 5, 6, 10 and 13,
Table 2). Alkyl groups may also be introduced as the
R
2 group (entry 8, Table 2), although the yield was
lower. In order to further clarify the structure of this
compound, we attempted the condensation reaction
of 2n with 2,4-dinitrophenylhydrazine to afford a solid
product ( E,Z)-4a, whose X-ray single crystal diffrac-
tion study definitely showed that the product 2n is
6,6,6,7-tetrafluoro-4-butyl-2-phenyl-2-heptenal in the
E,Z-configuration (Figure 1).
[16]
In order to further extend the scope, 4-methyl-2-
phenyl-2,3-pentadienol 1p and 5,5,5-trifluoro-4-
methyl-2-phenyl-2,3-pentadienol 1q were prepared [17]
and submitted to the standard conditions, respectively.
Interestingly, the reaction of 4-trifluoromethyl-substi-
tuted substrate 1q led to the similar aldehyde product

Conclusions
In summary, we have observed a unique C =C migra-
tion of 4-electron-withdrawing group-substituted 2,3-
allenols, which provides an efficient synthesis of 4-
electron-withdrawing group-substituted 2( E)-enals.
Due to the easy availability of the starting allenols,
[14]
and the highly functionalized nature of the products,
this method would be useful in organic synthesis.
Based on a careful mechanistic study, a possible
mechanism has been proposed. Further studies in this
area are being carried out in our laboratory.

Experimental Section
Materials
THF and Et 2O were distilled from Na/benzophenone before
use. MeCN and DCM were distilled from CaH 2 before use.
PhMgCl (1.8 M solution in THF) was purchased from Acros.
Other Grignard reagents were prepared from the corre-
sponding aryl halides and magnesium. Other commercially
available chemicals were purchased and used without addi-
tional purification unless noted otherwise.
1H NMR spectra
were recorded on a Bruker-300 MHz spectrometer and
13C NMR spectra were recorded at 75 MHz. All 1H NMR
experiments were measured with tetramethylsilane (0 ppm)
in CDCl 3 as the internal reference and 13C NMR experi-
ments were measured in relative to the signal of CDCl 3
(77.0 ppm) in CDCl 3. Due to the coupling of multiple fluo-
rines, 13C NMR signals of perfluoroalkyl group are extreme-
ly weak, and 19F NMR experiments were undecoupled and
measured relative to the signal of residual CFCl 3 (0 ppm) in
CDCl3. The coupling constant in the 1H NMR spectra larger
than 30 Hz is the H,F coupling.
